summary:
Mapte is a web prototype for planning and simulating scientific walks by astronauts on Mars. It covers a 10 × 10 km area of Mount Sharp in Gale Crater and addresses one key question: can a crew add a science stop and still return to base with sufficient reserves?
Mission Control configures the base, stops, walking speed, slope limits, and life-support budget on a 2D map. An A* planner operates on a 4 m grid derived from the USGS/HiRISE 1 m elevation model. It calculates each route segment and verifies the return journey before accepting a stop. If a stop is rejected, the system explains which constraint was exceeded.
Astronauts follow the same plan through a 3D explorer featuring heading, radar, and an elevation profile. At each stop, they can view authentic Curiosity photographs and see scientific findings.
Mapte addresses NASA's "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" challenge by integrating terrain data, orbital imagery, Curiosity photographs, and geological information into an actionable map. This approach supports future missions by providing routes that are not only safe but also explainable and traceable to their original data sources, helping crews make informed decisions while exploring Mars.
details:
Mapte plans astronaut walks across a 10 × 10 km area of Mount Sharp, in Gale Crater. Mission Control sets a base, science stops, a slope limit, a walking speed and a life-support budget. An A* planner finds routes on a 4 m grid built from the USGS/HiRISE elevation model. Before it accepts a stop, it checks the return to base and the reserve, and it says why when it drops one.

Benefits: the planner explains every decision, the data can be traced to its sources, and a single shared plan goes from planning to the walk itself.

Impact: teams can compare routes and their support costs before a walk, with each stop tied to real rover evidence.

Tools: TypeScript, React, OpenLayers, Three.js, Vite PWA, Python, FastAPI, SQLite, GDAL and NumPy. It runs in any browser with WebGL. Claude and Codex were used as coding assistants.

Creativity: it turns terrain into walking rules. Each stop has to fit the time and support budget, and it is backed by real Curiosity photos.

Factors considered: safety first, terrain with no data is never assumed safe, all layers share one map grid, it works offline, and it is clear about its limits: dust, temperature and radiation aren't modeled.
projectRefs: MSL Gale Merged DEM Mosaic, 1 m (USGS Astrogeology, HiRISE)
